You are worker FO1 in OPUS-CAPACITY-CAMPAIGN-20260908, an EMC research campaign. Your paper is `research/manuscripts/fusion-output/nr4a3-fusion-transcriptional-output.md` (PUB-FUSION-OUTPUT) — a drafted, unpublished manuscript not previously assigned in this campaign. Nobody else is working on it. Its SI is `nr4a3-fusion-transcriptional-output-SI.md`; read it as a source, but the main paper is your subject.

FIRST: read in full `/home/user/Rare-cancers/research/autonomy/opus-capacity-campaign-20260908/COMMON-BRIEF.md`, `CORPUS-CONTEXT.md` and `CLOSED-WORK.md`.

WRITE ISOLATION: READ-ONLY with respect to `/home/user/Rare-cancers`. Write nothing there, no git write, no edit to any manuscript, artifact, graph file, view or report. Scratch under `/tmp/claude-0/fo1-lane/` only; DO NOT delete it. Record `date -u`, `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` at start AND end; HEAD moves as the parent commits, so verify rather than assume.

MODEL: report your model as SELF-REPORT, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, and paste the literal output of `env | grep -i -E 'claude|anthropic|model' | sed -E 's/(TOKEN|KEY|SECRET)[^=]*=.*/\1=<redacted>/I'`.

TASK. This paper's own title says almost every gene set reads higher in the index arm, and it presents a size-matched empirical null. That makes it a paper about whether its null is adequate, so:

1. For each result it reports, quote the load-bearing sentence and read the committed artifact behind it.
2. Verdict: SUPPORTED AT THE STATED LEVEL, OVERSTATED (say what the source supports instead), MISATTRIBUTED, or NO SOURCE LOCATED.
3. For the null specifically: state what the null controls for and what it does not, as the artifacts describe it, and check whether the prose claims more.

The failure modes to hunt:
- **a set-level enrichment read as a biological finding when the paper's own null says the direction is generic** — the title concedes this, so check that every downstream claim honours it;
- **a repo-curated gene group presented as a published signature.** If the paper scores groups from `emc-expression-panels.json`, every panel there carries a `provenance` field reading "REPO-CURATED pathway-membership list. This is NOT a published gene set or signature. Any statement resting on it must say so" — check whether the prose says so;
- **a cohort or platform difference read as a disease difference**, and any claim that two arrays or two specimen labels are different patients when that is not established;
- **a missing measurement reported as zero** — a missing measurement is UNKNOWN, never zero.

Note two closed items you must NOT reopen: GSE4303 and GSE28866 are heavily retained and previously analysed, with no new cohort read, header read or availability correction admitted; different arrays or specimen labels are not proof of different patients. Read the existing records; run no new analysis and no retrieval.

Check every numeric quantity in the main text against the committed artifact leaf that should hold it: MATCH / MISMATCH (both values) / NO SOURCE LOCATED, with the exact key path you read. The paper's SI carries a known open finding — an `[]` empty-bracket cell in a driver column, baselined in `submission-residue-baseline.json` as "A REAL HOLE, NOT A CONVENTION" — do NOT try to fill it; if the main text depends on that cell, say so.

For every defect, propose EXACT replacement text as a single-occurrence string replacement (old verbatim, new verbatim). Apply nothing yourself.

PROHIBITIONS: author, propose as code, or apply no repair, patch, gate or test. Do not weaken, relax or reorder any guard, and do not edit or propose editing `submission-residue-baseline.json` or `pinned-figures.json`. Do not run `scripts/preflight.sh`, any producer or any figure generator. No network, no paid API, no GPU, no publication. Do not read, audit, extend or reference `reports/W25-*` or any W25 continuation. Contact no humans.

SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY (binding): no invented facts, sources, patient data, clinical efficacy/safety/therapeutic-window claims or test results. Distinguish primary evidence, prediction, association and experimental validation; preserve provenance and negative findings. Preregistrations are immutable. There is no wet lab: make no EMC efficacy, safety, selectivity or clinical-readiness claim. Absence of a located source is NOT evidence a claim is false. An approximation marker matters: a rounded value against a more precise source is a precision refinement, not a numeric error. If any request of yours is refused by content policy, STOP that branch, record the refusal verbatim, and never route around it.

Your verdict is specific to THIS paper. No repository census, no readiness claim about any other manuscript.

Stop condition: every result and every main-text quantity has a verdict, or ~45 tool calls. Returning early is a success; padding is not.

Report entirely in your final message. Headings: Worker / Question / Method and inputs / Result table with verdicts / What the null controls for, and what it does not / Quantity table with verdicts / Defects found, with exact proposed replacements / Limitations / Stop condition / Tool-call count actually used.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- aixiv-submission: Post a paper from this repository to aiXiv and read its automated review. Load before submitting or revising anything on aixiv.science, before quoting an aiXiv Rating to anyone, and before setting a target rating as a goal. Covers the working mechanics (agent token, the exactly-three category contract, metadata generated from the manuscript, PREFLIGHT_FULL before any post) and the three traps that cost a day: is_public=0 does NOT make a submission private, the Rating is written by an UNAUTHENTICATED endpoint so it is not a quality measurement, and ELEVEN versions of one paper never moved it above 6 — trending DOWN as the paper improved, until the target was abandoned by decision — while a DIFFERENT paper of the right shape scored 7 on its first version. Also the one thing that does move a rating (pick the paper, do not iterate the prose), why the review TEXT is worth having even though the number is not, the version-numbering and review-latency mechanics (the server assigns the version; 1.9 was followed by 2.0), and what this repository will not do to raise a number.
- ci-escape-hatches: How to route work OUT of this dev sandbox instead of deferring it. Load the moment you are about to write or think "I can't run X here", "no GPU/network/pip here", "this is blocked", "I can't test this locally", or you hit a 403 at the egress proxy (NCBI, GEO, PMC, EuropePMC, UniProt, Springer all block CONNECT). Also load before dispatching a GitHub Actions workflow, running a feature branch's CI without merging, timing a CI step, supervising a billing fleet, or setting up a self-wake poller. Covers: the two standing escape hatches (Actions runner for networked/CPU/PDF/pip work, spot GPU for heavy compute); workflow_dispatch with ref=<branch>; why the jobs API lag manufactures fake stalls; why a schedule: cron does not supervise a billing fleet; the fleet-armed heartbeat gate; retiring the non-file half of a feature; background-bash self-wake pollers; and GitHub auth/commit-signature noise that is safe to ignore.
- eli5: Explain something in plain language, the way you would to a smart person who does not work on this project. Load when the user types /eli5, or asks for it in their own words — "explain it like a normal person", "in plain English", "I don't follow", "assume I know nothing", "what does that actually mean" — or when they push back on an answer that was dense rather than wrong. Covers the rewrite rules (lead with the point, one idea per sentence, jargon gets replaced not glossed, at most one analogy), what plain language must NOT change (a hedge, a null, an unknown or a number stays exactly as strong as it was), and the failure modes that make an eli5 worse than the original — talking down, hollowing out, and the analogy that quietly becomes the argument.
- gpu-compute: Rules and hard-won provider facts for spending real GPU money — renting a host, launching a fleet or fan-out, picking a provider, pricing a rung, or diagnosing a job that stalled, died or kept billing. Load BEFORE any rental, relaunch, fleet launch or market gate, before writing a job that checkpoints, and before diagnosing a Vast or GCP provisioning, quota, capacity or teardown problem. Covers: never build an environment on a machine we are paying for (the baked Docker images and the parity reading); checkpoint-and-upload-continuously; default every GPU run to spot; serialize only when one result could cancel the rest; Vast capacity refusals, the retired durable machine blacklist, the $/ns market gate and board-depth holds; a relaunch is a new purchase and faces the same ceiling; the host cannot stop its own billing; GCP us-central1-only, GPUS_ALL_REGIONS=1 and the VMs-do-not-self-delete correction.
- inflight-reporting: The exact format of the end-of-turn "In flight" board, and the $/ns drift line that doubles as the buy line. Load whenever your final message will leave real compute running (GPU or CI jobs, subagents doing real work), when you need to decide whether a row gets a $/ns column at all, or when you are about to rent, relaunch or refuse a host on price. Covers: one scannable line per item with state, ET ETA, cost and $/ns against its basis; cost is part of the format, not an extra; the absolute buy line $0.006539/ns (approximately 1.92x basis) and why it is an absolute rate rather than a multiple; the drift line IS the buy line, a hard gate; and why a row we are paying and a row the gate refused must never render alike.
- paper-hardening: Review a research manuscript or verify a repair against its evidence, with a finite scope and a concrete submission decision.
- repo-gates: Run the repository checks appropriate to a code, evidence, or manuscript change and preserve an honest validation result.
- research-loop: Run one bounded EMC research cycle, select a useful deliverable, claim ownership, and preserve the outcome without overlapping writers.

Load BEFORE drafting or revising any manuscript, SI, cover letter or abstract that will go to a preprint server, a journal or aiXiv, and before applying a hardening round's findings to prose. Covers the four moves that carry almost all the gain (topic and stress positions, characters as subjects, actions as verbs, one sentence one idea), the revision pass that finds the damage, and the two failure modes that make a "clearer" paper worse — a hedge quietly dropped to shorten a sentence, and a readability score chased as a target. Metrics are a SCREEN that says where to look, never a measure of whether the prose is good; `lint_readability.py` reports, this file decides.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

46	# Almost every gene set reads higher in the index arm: a size-matched empirical null for small rare-tumour expression series, and what it leaves of the EWSR1::NR4A3 direct-target catalogue
47	
48	**Running title:** A size-matched null for rare-tumour gene-set reads
49	
50	**Author:** Tristan D. McRae¹
51	
52	¹ Independent Researcher. Correspondence: trimcrae@gmail.com
53	ORCID: [0000-0002-1823-1451](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1823-1451)
54	
55	**Article type:** Original Research Article
56	**Keywords:** empirical null; gene-set calibration; small-sample expression analysis; rare sarcoma; extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma; EWSR1::NR4A3; transcriptional target
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Abstract
61	
62	On a small rare-tumour expression series, almost every gene set anyone scores comes back higher in
63	the index arm. In a 10-versus-6 extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) series, PPARγ targets,
64	hypoxia metagenes and adipogenesis all move alike. The reason is size, not biology: a set's
65	per-sample score is one draw from a distribution whose width depends on the set's **size** and on the
66	platform, so an arbitrary set can print t = 3.16 and be indistinguishable from a random one of the
67	same size. **We supply the
68	calibration that refuses such a read** — a size-matched empirical null drawn from the platform's own
69	genes — and apply it to this disease's best-warranted set. Across 2,276 retrieved documents, **the
70	set with a DNA-binding assay against an NR4A3 chimera is three genes: *SEMA3C*, *PPARG*, *ENO3***.
71	Three is below the four-gene floor for a set score, so the set scored is those three pooled with the
72	sixteen native-NR4A3 targets. On the two readable array platforms **that pooled set reaches 39% and
73	88% of its null threshold and does not clear**, while the published EMC phenotype clears it 11.9-fold
74	and 4.2-fold in the same run — the instrument reads this disease, not this set. Exact label
75	permutation, every comparator stratum separately, a matrix covariate and a muscle control then
76	separate the three: *SEMA3C* survives nothing and reverses sign with the comparator; *PPARG*'s
77	strongest reading is circular, scored on the cohort that first published it; *ENO3* survives
78	everything, but was the pre-designated positive control and is not an independent finding here.
79	**The binding constraint is not sample size.** No experiment has measured where an NR4A3 fusion binds,
80	or what chromatin does, in EMC material — the one genome-wide chromatin readout that exists for these
81	fusions reads *accessibility* in HEK293T (GSE243553), and the 110 NR4A peak sets that exist are the
82	wrong protein or the wrong disease, with no class-A gene carrying unusual occupancy against a
83	background panel. Until a fusion cistrome in EMC chromatin exists, "elevated in EMC" and "driven by
84	the fusion" are inseparable. The null is not EMC-specific: any series with a small index arm and
85	heterogeneous comparators fails the same way.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 1 · Introduction
90	
91	### 1.1 · Almost every gene set reads higher in the index arm
92	
93	A rare tumour affords a small index arm and a heterogeneous comparator arm, and on such a series
94	almost every gene set anyone scores comes back higher in the index arm. In the series this paper
95	works with — 10 extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcomas (EMC) against 6 comparators, GSE4303 on platform
96	GPL3290 — PPARγ targets, hypoxia metagenes, adipogenesis, chondroitin-sulfate biosynthesis and
97	arginine metabolism all come back "higher in EMC". Sets with no biological relationship to one
98	another move the same way and by similar amounts.
99	
100	The reason is not biology. A raw Welch contrast on the sample means uses the samples as its unit of
101	variability and ignores that a set's per-sample score is one draw from a distribution whose width
102	depends on the set's *size* and on the platform. At n = 10 versus 6 that width is large: the 95% band
103	for an arbitrary 17-gene set on GPL3290 is [−0.297, +0.376] SD, so a set can print t = 3.16 and remain
104	indistinguishable from a random set of the same size. Seventeen is the size scored there: the pooled
105	direct-target set names nineteen genes, and that platform reads two of them, *ICAM1* and *MYH7*, on
106	no probe.
107	
108	**No read on such a series is interpretable until it is calibrated against a size-matched random gene
109	set drawn from the same platform's own genes.** That calibration is the instrument this paper
110	supplies; it costs one seeded resampling, it is drawn in **Figure 1**, and it is applied to this
111	work's own headline result rather than only to other people's. **It is not specific to this disease
112	or this gene set** — any series with a small index arm and a heterogeneous comparator arm has the
113	same failure mode, and rare tumours are where such series are the only ones that exist.
114	
115	The rest of the paper is that instrument applied to one worked example, chosen because it is the gene
116	set in this disease carrying the strongest mechanistic warrant, and because its literature is small
117	enough to enumerate exhaustively rather than sample. **The example is not the contribution**, and
118	§4.2 states which parts of it would and would not survive being wrong.
119	
120	### 1.2 · The disease and the driver
121	
122	EMC is a rare soft-tissue sarcoma defined by rearrangement of *NR4A3* (NOR-1/TEC). Subramanian *et al.*
123	describe it as "characterized by a balanced translocation most commonly involving t(9;22) (q22;q12)"
124	(PMID 15920699), which produces EWSR1::NR4A3; Brenca *et al.* express and assay both that chimera and
125	TAF15::NR4A3, "the commonest TAF15 (exons 1–6)–NR4A3 (exons 3–8) fusion" (PMID 31020999), with a
126	rarer *t(3;9)(q11-12;q22)* TFG::NR4A3 variant accounting for part of the remainder. NR4A3 is an orphan
127	nuclear receptor, and the chimera places its DNA-binding domain under a strong FET-family
128	transactivation domain. The disease's central molecular hypothesis is therefore straightforward: the
129	fusion is a transcription factor with an aberrant output, and that output is where the disease lives.
130	
131	### 1.3 · The gap in the worked example
132	
133	The hypothesis dates from the fusion's cloning in 1995 (PMID 8634690), and the evidence under it is
134	thin in a specific, checkable way. Two questions bear on it, and they are different questions:
135	
136	1. Which genes has anyone shown an NR4A3 chimera to physically bind and drive?
137	2. Which genes are high in EMC tumours?
138	
139	**Neither is much discussed.** Measured against Europe PMC on 2026-08-08: of 1,305 records naming the
140	disease, 261 are reviews, and the three genes with a published fusion DNA-binding assay are named in
141	**3, 1 and 0 of those 261 reviews** respectively (*PPARG*, *SEMA3C*, *ENO3*; 37, 6 and 2 records in
142	the corpus as a whole, and both *ENO3* records are about a different disease). The primary sources
143	are, by contrast, ordinary references of this literature — 42–70% of their citations come from EMC
144	records, and three of the four are cited by four to six EMC reviews. The fourth, the *ENO3* source,
145	is cited by none of them. So the gap this addresses is not a
146	contested claim in need of correction; it is that a disease defined by a transcription-factor fusion
147	has **no assembled account of what that fusion transcribes**, and the question is asked rarely enough
148	that the distinction between the two above has had little occasion to be drawn. Query strings,
149	counts and their limits are in the deposited probe artifact.
150	
151	The first is a mechanism claim; the second is an association. A gene can satisfy the second for reasons
152	that have nothing to do with the fusion — EMC's cell of origin, its myxoid and hypocellular
153	architecture, the anatomical site it arises in, or the gene being a generic matrix or proliferation
154	gene. This work separates the two by (a) cataloguing the mechanism claims with their evidence type
155	recorded per gene, (b) reading them back in tumour tissue with an explicit calibration for what an
156	arbitrary gene set does on the same platform, and (c) putting each gene through the specific
157	confounds that could have manufactured it.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## 2 · Materials and Methods
162	
163	Full method detail — probe mapping, scoring floors, the circularity grading procedure, the
164	pre-registered decision rule and the motif-scan parameters — is in Supplementary Information §S1–S6.
165	
166	### 2.1 · The evidence-typed target catalogue
167	
168	Every claim in the primary literature that EWSR1::NR4A3, another NR4A3 fusion, or native NR4A3
169	transcriptionally activates a named gene was recorded with: the gene, the factor actually tested, the
170	assays, the cell system, the species of those cells, the expected direction in EMC, and the verbatim
171	sentence the classification rests on. Rows were read from retrieved full text, not from memory. Four
172	evidence classes were assigned per row (**Table 1**; the complete 22-row catalogue with verbatim
173	sentences is Supplementary Table S1).
174	
175	**Table 1. The evidence classes, and how many genes are in each.**
176	
177	| class | definition | genes |
178	|---|---|---:|
179	| **A** — fusion DNA-binding | a DNA-binding or promoter assay performed **with an NR4A3 fusion**. The strongest class. | **3** |
180	| **B** — native DNA-binding | the same assay class with **native NR4A3**. Transfer to the fusion is an assumption. | 16 |
181	| **C** — fusion expression only | the gene moves when the fusion is expressed; no binding assay. | 2 |
182	| **D** — EMC tumour expression only | measured in EMC tissue; no mechanism. | 1 |
183	
184	### 2.2 · Datasets
185	
186	Three independent EMC cohorts on three platform families were used. They are never pooled (§5).
187	
188	**Table 2. The three cohorts.**
189	
190	| cohort | platform | EMC | comparators | value kind |
191	|---|---|---|---|---|
192	| **GSE24369** | GPL6244, Affymetrix Gene ST | 6 | 29 — 17 FET-rearranged LGFMS + 6 myxofibrosarcoma + 6 desmoid fibromatosis | single-channel intensity |
193	| **GSE4303** | GPL3290, 42,000-spot two-colour cDNA | 10 | 6 (3 DFSP + 3 GIST) | two-colour log-ratio vs a reference pool |
194	| **GSE28866** | 3SEQ (GPL10999) | 4 | 32 non-EMC sarcoma libraries; 27 normal-organ libraries | 3′-end read density per peak |
195	
196	Every class label above is the GEO sample title, not an internal grouping name. That distinction
197	decides §3.4: **23 of the 29 GPL6244 comparators are themselves myxoid tumours** — 17 low-grade
198	*fibromyxoid* sarcomas and 6 *myxo*fibrosarcomas — against 6 collagen-rich desmoid fibromatoses,
199	whereas none of the 6 GPL3290 comparators is myxoid. The two array cohorts therefore differ in the
200	one property the leading confound is built on, which makes the pair a natural control rather than
201	only a limitation.
202	
203	- **GSE24369** — its comparator arm is itself FET-rearranged (LGFMS is *FUS::CREB3L2*), so a difference
204	  here is not merely "has a FET fusion". The array carries 42 samples; 6 EMC + 29 comparators accounts
205	  for 35, and the remaining 7 — **five solitary fibrous tumours and two pooled skeletal-muscle RNA
206	  samples** — are excluded from both arms rather than silently absorbed into either, so the
207	  arithmetic closes. The two muscle samples are named here because they are not merely surplus:
208	  they are the reference that makes the *ENO3* muscle-admixture objection measurable (§3.5).
209	  Linked series PubMed identifier 21536545.
210	- **GSE4303** — Subramanian *et al.*, *J Pathol* 2005;206:433–444 (PMID 15920699). See §3.8 on
211	  circularity. Two structural facts about this deposit bear on every number read from it. It is a
212	  **seven-platform series** — seven sibling print runs of one clone library — of which only GPL3290
213	  carries a usable EMC-versus-comparator contrast, so the 10 versus 6 here is not the whole deposit.
214	  The **published** Subramanian cohort was 10 EMC against 26 other sarcomas, so a reader opening the
215	  accession will find comparators this analysis does not use. Separately, the verbatim sample
216	  annotations record the reference pool each two-colour hybridisation was run against: all 10 EMC
217	  and all 3 DFSP samples are on the CRH pool, while **the 3 GIST samples are on Universal Human
218	  Reference — a different pool** (§3.4).
219	- **GSE28866** — Brunner *et al.*, *Genome Biol* 2012;13(8):R75 (PMID 22929540). The EMC libraries are
220	  EMC_STT5525/5526/5527/5592; the normal arm is 27 libraries across six organs (bowel, breast, colon,
221	  kidney, lung, uterus). The 32 non-EMC sarcoma columns include two pairs of technical replicates of
222	  one specimen each (ESS_STT5520, LMS_STT516), so 32 libraries come from 30 specimens.
223	
224	Each cohort's EMC arm size in Table 2 was read from its series matrix. All three were separately
225	recovered from GEO **sample titles** — an independent path to the same numbers, 6, 10 and 4 — during
226	the cohort search of §2.7, where they serve as its positive control: a search that cannot find the
227	datasets that exist says nothing about the ones that do not.
228	
229	⚠ One deposit is not a fourth cohort and is easy to mistake for one. **GSE170983** carries 99
230	samples, four of them EMC, under its own accession — and it is the same Brunner deposit as GSE28866,
231	with the same four tumours (GSM715466/715467/715470/715472) and the same linked publication.
232	Counting the two separately would raise the apparent EMC total to 24 without adding a patient.
233	
234	### 2.3 · Scoring and the size-matched empirical null
235	
236	Probes were mapped to symbols per platform (GPL6244: 20,230 of 28,459 probes → 18,694 distinct
237	symbols; GPL3290: 27,203 of 43,008 probes → 14,932, through an EST-accession bridge). Each sample's
238	values were z-scored against that array's own probe distribution; a gene or set score for a sample is
239	the mean z over its readable members; the contrast is a Welch *t* on the EMC versus comparator
240	per-sample scores. **A gene with no probe is treated as an unread gene, never as an absent one.**
241	Floors were fixed at three samples per group for any contrast, and four genes / 0.4 coverage for any
242	set score.
243	
244	Two quantities a raw Welch contrast does not supply are computed per platform. **The exact global
245	offset** is the per-sample mean z over every symbol the platform maps, contrasted EMC versus
246	comparator — the amount by which an arbitrary gene set is expected to differ for no set-specific
247	reason. **The size-matched empirical null** is 4,000 random gene sets of exactly the observed size,
248	drawn from a seeded random pool of the platform's own mapped symbols (seed 20260807; pool 4,000;
249	universe 18,694 for GPL6244, 14,932 for GPL3290), each scored exactly as the real set is. A random set
250	carries the offset too, so the null absorbs it by construction. The empirical p is the **two-sided**
251	fraction of draws at least as extreme, with +1/+1 smoothing. A set is reported as SET-SPECIFIC only
252	if the observed delta falls outside the 95% band of that null; single genes are calibrated the same
253	way at set size 1.
254	
255	**The empirical p has a floor, and it is quoted as one.** With 4,000 draws and +1/+1 smoothing the
256	smallest two-sided value the design can return is 2/4001 = 0.0005, and every such value below is
257	written **`p_emp ≤ 0.0005`** — the resolution limit of the null, not a measured value. The floor is
258	not the same on both platforms. A draw is discarded when the gene it picks leaves either arm below
259	the three-sample contrast floor, so every size-1 null on GPL3290 retains 3,700 of its 4,000 draws and
260	its floor there is 2/3701 = 0.00054, the value Table 4 prints for *ENO3*.
261	Three further limits of the pool are stated rather than left implied: it is a **seeded 4,000-symbol
262	random subsample** of each platform's mapped symbols (21% of GPL6244's 18,694, 27% of GPL3290's
263	14,932), the same pool is reused at every set size, and the gene under test is not excluded from it.
264	
265	The null's own limit is stated rather than assumed: it is a **competitive** null, controlling for the
266	platform-wide offset and for set *size*, but not for gene–gene correlation inside a real pathway. It
267	is therefore anti-conservative for coherent sets and is a screen, not a test — which is why §2.6
268	supplies a self-contained null alongside it.
269	
270	### 2.4 · Instrument controls, graded before the biology
271	
272	Four known answers were graded before any biological read. The first two are ***ENO3*** (UP on both
273	platforms — the positive control) and ***NR4A3*** (UP — tumour identity). The other two are
274	***PLAGL1*** (DOWN, PMID 16112421 — the directional falsifier, the only prediction an arm-wide
275	offset cannot manufacture) and ***SGK1*** (flat or down at transcript level despite 10/10 protein
276	positivity, PMID 16756948 — the only row whose published transcript and protein directions oppose).
277	
278	Grading is on where the delta sits relative to its size-1 null, never on the raw delta. **The rule has
279	three outcomes, not two, and the third is the one that needs stating.** A reading whose delta falls
280	*outside* its null band is graded, and agrees or disagrees with the published direction. A reading
281	whose delta falls *inside* the band is **not a reading at this power** and is not graded either way —
282	a randomly chosen gene on that platform would land there too. And a control with no computable
283	contrast at all (for example, *NR4A3* on GPL3290, where four of six comparator spots for that probe
284	are missing, leaving two values against a floor of three) is likewise not graded.
285	
286	Two consequences follow, and both are reported rather than left for a reader to find. First, the
287	denominator of any "n of n agree" statement is the number of **gradeable readings**, not the number
288	of controls — §3.3 gives both. Second, a control can only fail by landing outside its band in the
289	*wrong* direction, so a control with a wide band is weakly falsifiable; §3.3 therefore prints each
290	control's band beside its verdict, because a prediction that could not have been refused is not
291	evidence that it was tested. An absent reading is not a reading of absence, and the block whose job
292	is to tell a working instrument from a broken one is the last place that distinction may collapse.
293	
294	### 2.5 · The 3SEQ arm, and its calibration
295	
296	3SEQ measures 3′-end read density per peak. A gene's value in a library is the median across that
297	gene's peaks; an arm's value is the median across that arm's libraries. **No z-score, no test and no
298	confidence interval are used, because n = 4.** 3SEQ read density is not array intensity, and nothing
299	from this arm is pooled with the arrays.
300	
301	A fold-change is not a reading until an arbitrary gene's fold-change is known, so the same two ratios
302	were computed for **every gene in the deposit** (14,120 genes; 13,708 with a computable EMC/normal
303	ratio, 13,247 with an EMC/sarcoma ratio) and each target gene is reported as a **percentile of that
304	distribution**. A gene whose comparator median is zero has no ratio and is excluded from the
305	distribution rather than ranked at the top. A percentile is a rank, not a p-value, and none is implied.
306	
307	### 2.6 · Confound audit and sensitivity analyses
308	
309	Four further readings were computed offline from the same cached inputs, all using the same scoring
310	primitives so the quantity tested is identical to the quantity reported. Every delta re-derived here
311	was asserted equal to the primary artifact before anything was written.
312	
313	1. **Exact sample-label permutation** (a self-contained null). The EMC/comparator label is permuted
314	   over samples and the *real* gene set rescored, so correlation structure is carried through
315	   untouched. Arm sizes give 1,623,160 and 8,008 distinct assignments — few enough to **enumerate
316	   completely**, so every reported p is exact rather than sampled. Two-sided throughout.
317	2. **Every comparator stratum, separately.** The contrast is recomputed with the comparator arm
318	   restricted to one class at a time, to the myxoid classes only, to the non-myxoid classes only,
319	   and — on GPL3290 — to the **reference-pool-matched** comparators only. Nothing about the EMC arm
320	   or the reduction changes, so any movement is attributable to who is in the comparator arm. Each
321	   stratified contrast carries its own exact permutation p (C(29,6) = 475,020 down to
322	   C(13,10) = 286, all enumerated completely).
323	3. **Covariate-adjusted sensitivity.** Each gene's per-sample z is regressed on a matrix-content
324	   proxy and the contrast recomputed on the residuals. **The proxy is selected by provenance:** every
325	   candidate is checked against every gene this manuscript scores anywhere, and any gene drawn from
326	   an EMC-derived list is refused, because adjusting on a gene selected *because* it is high in EMC
327	   removes EMC signal by construction. Two panels survive that filter: 11 structural genes
328	   (*BGN, COL5A1, COL5A2, DCN, FN1, LUM, MMP2, POSTN, SPP1, TNC, VIM*) and 3 vascular genes (*ENG,
329	   KDR, TEK*). The structural panel is the one §3.6 reports first; the vascular panel's reading is
330	   reported beside it, because the two do not agree on GPL3290. This is
331	   a sensitivity analysis, not a correction: a proxy that is itself downstream of the fusion would
332	   over-adjust, and that possibility is not excluded.
333	4. **The skeletal-muscle admixture control** (§3.5), plus a **leave-one-out jackknife** over the EMC
334	   arm, a **rank-based re-read** on within-array percentile, and **Benjamini–Hochberg** q-values
335	   across the per-gene permutation p-values within each platform.
336	5. **NR4A occupancy** (§3.11). The scan intersected 110 published NR4A ChIP-seq peak sets —
337	   ChIP-Atlas, ReMap2022 and the Haller *et al.* acinic cell carcinoma deposit — with the class-A
338	   genes' regulatory windows, the same window as the motif scan, so the sequence and occupancy axes
339	   ask about one region. Every count was placed against a background panel of 198 genes assembled
340	   for an unrelated question. Four rules govern the reading. A **raw count is never reported as a
341	   finding**, because the deepest catalogue puts a peak in 82.8% of the panel. A peak set that
342	   recovers (almost) no panel gene is marked **uninformative**: it cannot fail to recover these
343	   three, so its silence is an absent reading and is never counted as evidence of non-occupancy.
344	   **Only NR4A antigens are scored** — the Haller deposit also carries CTCF, H3K27ac, H3K27me3,
345	   H3K4me3 and super-enhancer calls, and a histone peak at a promoter reports that the promoter is
346	   active, not that an NR4A protein is there. And the nominal-hit count is judged by a **binomial
347	   tail** against the number of tests rather than by comparing an integer to a fractional
348	   expectation. Multiplicity is over distinct **experiments**, not genome builds, since the same
349	   experiment appears once per build.
350	
351	   The Haller peak files carry no genome build, and a BED intersected on an assumed build does not
352	   fail — on chr10 it silently reports another locus. The build was therefore **measured**: H3K4me3
353	   marks active promoters, so on the correct build it must recover most of the same background panel
354	   and on the wrong one it must not. All four samples independently gave **90.6–93.9% panel recovery
355	   on hg19 against 32.2–33.6% on hg38**, and the deposit is read as hg19. Both an absolute floor
356	   (0.80) and a ratio (2.0) are required, because the two builds agree over much of the genome, so
357	   ~33% is the expected wrong-build floor rather than noise.
358	
359	### 2.7 · The cohort search
360	
361	Six deliberately overlapping queries were put to GEO — the disease name in full and abbreviated, the
362	fusion rather than the disease, the 3′ partner plus lineage, and two over-broad terms chosen to
363	return pan-sarcoma and general chondrosarcoma deposits in which EMC samples might sit under a generic
364	title. Every query is recorded with its own stated purpose, including any returning nothing, because
365	a query that returns nothing is indistinguishable from a dataset that does not exist unless the query
366	itself is on the record.
367	
368	Three properties of the procedure matter more than the queries. **Every returned series is read at
369	sample level**, not screened on its title: GEO titles are depositors' claims, and GSE24369 — titled
370	after low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma while carrying six EMC tumours — is the standing demonstration
371	that a title-level screen would discard the very cohorts this analysis rests on. **Every candidate is
372	deduplicated at three levels** — accession, linked publication, and sample identity against all 157
373	GSM records the three cohorts read — because a re-deposit under a new accession is otherwise
374	indistinguishable from a new cohort. And **the search is graded against a positive control**: the
375	three cohorts already in use must be recovered by the same queries, with their EMC arm sizes, or the
376	result is withheld as uninterpretable rather than reported as a negative.
377	
378	### 2.8 · Reproduction
379	
380	Every value in §3 derives from a committed artifact and is not re-typed from prose. All analyses are
381	CPU-only, use open-source tooling, and reproduce offline from cached inputs with no network access;
382	producers refuse to write if any row disagrees with the artifact that owns it. See Data and code
383	availability.

673	### 3.10 · A sequence axis, and its limits
674	
675	NR4A3's monomer site is the NBRE, 5′-AAAGGTCA-3′ (PMID 1902986); the dimer site is the NurRE
676	(PMID 9315667). A TSS-centred window of −10 kb/+15 kb — fixed in advance on published regulatory
677	architecture, before any sequence was read — was scanned on both strands with positional
678	de-duplication, and calibrated against a dinucleotide-preserving shuffle of the same window (2,000
679	shuffles, holding GC and CpG content exactly) and a 198-window background panel assembled for an
680	unrelated question. Full parameters and the one-mismatch analysis are in Supplementary §S6.
681	
682	***ENO3* carries 4 exact NBREs, more than its own composition predicts** (shuffle-null p = 0.034;
683	GC-matched background p = 0.018). *PPARG* carries 3, which is what composition predicts (p = 0.227).
684	***SEMA3C* carries none.** The background panel averages 1.15 exact NBREs per 25 kb window, so a
685	single hit is what an arbitrary window contains anyway.
686	
687	Four things this does not establish. **A motif is not occupancy**, and the chromatin experiment that
688	would test it now exists, was run, and does not support these sites. Frenkel *et al.* expressed
689	EWSR1-NR4A3, TAF15-NR4A3, TCF12-NR4A3 and TFG-NR4A3 in HEK293T inside a pooled variant library and
690	resolved each one's effect on chromatin accessibility by single-cell ATAC (GSE243553;
691	PMID 39048711). Their per-fusion accessibility calls were intersected with the four exact NBRE
692	coordinates above on the matching genome build — the deposit declares hg38 and these coordinates are
693	GRCh38, so no lift-over was required. **Three of the four sites fall inside TAF15-NR4A3's called
694	intervals and none falls inside EWSR1-NR4A3's.** Neither observation supports the motif argument.
695	The EWSR1-NR4A3 set is too sparse for its zero to be a reading: it recovers 2 of 203 promoters in a
696	background gene panel assembled for an unrelated question, so a chosen gene could not have been
697	recovered either. The TAF15-NR4A3 co-location does not clear a null that slides the same four-site
698	configuration, at its true spacing, to a random offset within the same window (*p* = 0.08, 20,000
699	seeded draws). That null is the one that matters here because two of the four sites are 153 bp apart
700	and a single 500 bp interval covers both; nulls treating them as independent return *p* ≤ 0.002 and
701	overstate the result by a factor of about forty. The TFG-NR4A3 arm — the fusion Kim *et al.* used
702	for the published *ENO3* result — is likewise too sparse to grade. ⛔ Three conditions bound all of
703	this: the cells are HEK293T and not EMC chromatin, accessibility is not binding, and *ENO3* is this
704	study's own pre-designated positive control (§2.4), so a hit there would have been a check on the
705	instrument rather than a discovery. **The sequence axis and the chromatin axis have now been made to
706	meet at these coordinates, and they do not corroborate each other.** Method, seeds and the four
707	nulls: [`gse243553-eno3-overlap-2026-08-08.md`](gse243553-eno3-overlap-2026-08-08.md). **The
708	*SEMA3C* zero does not contradict Brenca *et al.***, who report a predicted NBRE-*like* site assayed
709	by ChAP-qPCR; an NBRE-like site is by construction not an exact NBRE. That class was therefore
710	scanned too, and *SEMA3C*'s 39 one-mismatch sites — the most of any gene scanned — are **exactly
711	what its own composition predicts** (null mean 33.7, p = 0.203; GC-matched p = 0.118), with only the
712	composition-naive raw rank suggesting enrichment (p = 0.040) in the most AT-rich window of the set.
713	**The hit positions do not reproduce the published coordinates** for either *ENO3* or *PPARG*, both
714	of which numbered from their own promoter constructs. **A distal element outside the window is
715	untested by construction** — while the elements *inside* the window have now been tested against an
716	orthogonal instrument, and were not corroborated by it.

973	## 4 · Discussion
974	
975	### 4.1 · What these data are consistent with, and what they are equally consistent with
976	
977	A target gene that is up in EMC is consistent with the fusion driving it, and equally consistent with:
978	(a) EMC's cell of origin expressing it; (b) EMC's myxoid, hypocellular architecture; (c) a
979	platform-wide offset; (d) the gene being a generic proliferation or matrix gene; (e) the anatomical
980	site EMC arises in.
981	
982	This version narrows more of that list than its predecessor did. The null calibration removes (c)
983	and part of (d). **(b) is now partly measured rather than conceded**. The GPL6244 comparator arm is
984	23/29 myxoid, so it is largely matched to EMC on matrix architecture, and *ENO3* is unchanged
985	against the myxoid-only arm (+0.808, p = 8 × 10⁻⁵). Adjusting for an 11-gene matrix proxy chosen to
986	contain no EMC-selected gene leaves 75% of its delta where the covariate differs between arms and
987	100% where it does not. **(e) is bounded for *ENO3*** by the muscle control of §3.5. What remains
988	genuinely unremoved is **(a)**: nothing in these datasets separates a gene the fusion drives from a
989	gene EMC's cell of origin expresses, and the 3SEQ normal-organ arm does not help, because six
990	visceral organs are not the soft tissue EMC arises in.
991	
992	### 4.2 · What is new here
993	
994	Four things, in descending order of what survives this paper's own worked example being wrong.
995	Nothing here is a first-in-field claim.
996	
997	- **The calibration, which is the contribution.** A size-matched empirical null on the platform's own
998	  genes converts a pervasive and uninformative "higher in the index arm" into a statement that can be
999	  refused — and it refuses this work's own aggregate, at a quantified distance (39% and 88% of
1000	  threshold) rather than as a bare negative. It costs one seeded resampling. **It is not specific to
1001	  EMC, to this gene set, or to these three cohorts**: any series with a small index arm and a
1002	  heterogeneous comparator arm has the same failure mode, and in rare tumours such series are the
1003	  only ones that exist. Every biological claim below could be overturned tomorrow by a cistrome
1004	  without touching this.
1005	- **The map of what is missing, and the experiment that closes it.** Class A is three genes wide.
1006	  Nothing has been deposited on EMC material under any chromatin library strategy, so no experiment
1007	  has measured where an NR4A3 fusion binds or what chromatin does in EMC chromatin. The same
1008	  archives, meanwhile, hold chromatin maps for EWSR1::WT1, EWSR1::ATF1, EWSR1::FLI1, FUS::DDIT3 and
1009	  HEY1::NCOA2, and one *accessibility* screen carrying four NR4A3 fusions in HEK293T (GSE243553).
1010	  And the 110 NR4A peak sets that do exist are measured — not assumed — to be unable to substitute
1011	  (§3.11). §4.3 then names the discriminating experiment rather than gesturing at one. For a disease
1012	  with no fusion cistrome, a specified missing experiment is a more useful output than another
1013	  correlative reading, and it is the part of this paper addressed to anyone with a laboratory.
1014	- **The confound audit.** Comparator composition read from the GEO sample titles rather than from a
1015	  grouping label; the contrast recomputed against every stratum, against the reference-pool-matched
1016	  comparators, and against a provenance-filtered matrix covariate; and a skeletal-muscle control for
1017	  the one gene where that objection is obvious.
1018	- **The ordering, which is the worked example and the weakest part.** The three genes are not equally
1019	  supported: *SEMA3C* is supported by nothing that survives its own comparator being varied, and

1020	  *PPARG*'s strongest reading is circular. ⚠ **The surviving gene is the pre-designated positive
1021	  control** (Limitation 17), so *ENO3*'s elevation is not an independent finding of this work, and
1022	  the ordering rests on three cohorts of 4, 6 and 10. Read it as a demonstration that the instrument
1023	  discriminates where a raw contrast does not — not as a settled biology.
1024	
1025	A note on what is *not* claimed. No prior source states the class-A count of three, but the reason is
1026	measured rather than asserted (§1.3), and it is not that the field says something different: the
1027	three genes are named in 3, 1 and 0 of 261 EMC review records, so there is no competing account to
1028	correct. ⚠ **That is a claim about a near-absence, the weaker of the two directions a citation index
1029	supports.** Seldom-named is a positive reading; *no source anywhere assembles them* is not
1030	established by it, and a review outside the searched corpus could do so.
1031	
1032	### 4.3 · What would discriminate, named rather than hand-waved
1033	
1034	1. **A cistrome in the right cell.** An NR4A3 ChIP-seq peak set with the *fusion* expressed,
1035	   intersected with these expression reads: a gene that is up in EMC *and* carries a fusion-bound NBRE
1036	   is driven; a gene that is up with no peak is correlated. The nearest existing dataset is Haller
1037	   *et al.* (2019, *Nat Commun* 10:368, PMID 30664630): NR4A3 ChIP-seq in three human acinic cell
1038	   carcinoma tumours, with a de-novo NBRE motif recovered in all three (processed data on Zenodo, doi
1039	   10.5281/zenodo.1483691; raw data on EGA, EGAS00001002795, controlled access). The caveat is
1040	   load-bearing: acinic cell carcinoma carries *native* NR4A3 up-regulated by enhancer hijacking, not
1041	   a fusion. Given §3.2's measurement that native NR4A3 does not activate the *PPARG* promoter the
1042	   fusion does, that dataset answers "where does the NR4A3 DNA-binding domain go in a human tumour"
1043	   and not "where does EWSR1::NR4A3 go". It must never be cited as the latter. The nearest dataset in
1044	   which an NR4A3 *fusion* is the perturbation is GSE243553 (§3.11), and it is subject to the same
1045	   restriction from the other direction: it reads chromatin **accessibility** in HEK293T, not
1046	   occupancy in EMC chromatin, so it cannot be intersected with these expression reads to call a gene
1047	   driven. The experiment named here is occupancy of an NR4A3 fusion in EMC material, and §3.11 shows
1048	   the field performs exactly that experiment routinely for neighbouring fusions.
1049	2. **Fusion knockdown or degradation in a genuinely fusion-positive EMC model, with RNA-seq.** No such
1050	   experiment was retrieved.
1051	3. **Fusion-type-stratified EMC expression data.** Brenca *et al.* show class-3 versus class-4–6
1052	   semaphorins separating EWSR1- from TAF15-translocated EMC, but no readable series records which
1053	   fusion each EMC sample carries, so every EMC arm here is a mixture and any fusion-specific signal is
1054	   attenuated by an unknown amount.
1055	4. **A within-EMC test against fusion level was attempted and does not discriminate at this n.**
1056	   Holding disease constant and correlating each gene against *NR4A3* level inside the EMC arm is the
1057	   only axis in these data that speaks to fusion *output* rather than EMC membership. It gives
1058	   r = +0.37 (n = 6) and −0.35 (n = 9) for *ENO3* on the two platforms — opposite signs, no
1059	   information. The GPL3290 axis reads 9 of that arm's 10 tumours, because it is anchored on *NR4A3*
1060	   and one sample carries no readable *NR4A3* value. Reported so that the axis is not proposed again as though untried; *NR4A3* array
1061	   signal is in any case the 3′ partner under a foreign promoter, not the fusion transcript.
1062	5. **An NBRE motif scan** — performed (§3.10). It cannot demonstrate binding and did not resolve the
1063	   question. **What remains undone on this axis is not another scan**: sequence cannot settle
1064	   occupancy, and the discriminating experiment is item 1.

1068	## 5 · Limitations
1069	
1070	These are ceilings, not caveats: each one bounds what any sentence in §3 may be read to mean.
1071	
1072	1. **n = 4, 6 and 10 EMC.** Nothing here survives being described as a distribution, and no result
1073	   should be read as a population estimate. This is a ceiling on the disease, not on the search. A
1074	   term search of GEO returned 56 records, of which 22 were series or curated datasets; every one
1075	   was read at sample level, and none was a fourth EMC expression cohort. The seventeen unrelated
1076	   sarcoma and chondrosarcoma deposits among them carry no EMC sample between them (§3.13,
1077	   Table 10). The bound is what a term search can reach: a deposit naming the disease nowhere in
1078	   its GEO record is invisible to it, and no other archive was searched.
1079	2. **The three cohorts are never pooled, and must never be.** 3SEQ 3′-end read density is not array
1080	   intensity; single-channel intensity and two-colour log-ratio are not the same quantity either. The
1081	   concordance in §3.5–3.7 is sign agreement across three independent measurements, which is weaker
1082	   than a combined estimate and is deliberately reported as the weaker thing.
1083	3. **Transcript, not protein.** *SGK1* is the worked example: its published protein and transcript
1084	   directions oppose, and this instrument can only see the second.
1085	4. **No occupancy, and therefore no causality from the fusion.** Nothing here shows any gene being
1086	   bound by EWSR1::NR4A3 *in EMC*. The class-A assays were performed in engineered human fibroblasts,
1087	   in rat chondrogenic cells, and with a chimera (TFG::NR4A3) that is not the common one.
1088	5. **The normal arm is a six-organ tissue panel, not matched adjacent tissue**, so it cannot separate
1089	   EMC-specific from mesenchymal-lineage-specific.
1090	6. **Comparator arms differ between platforms.** §3.6 turns this into a designed contrast rather than
1091	   only a limitation, but the strata are small — 6 desmoids, 3 DFSP, 3 GIST — and a stratified
1092	   contrast at n = 3 comparators can report no p below 0.0035 however large the effect.
1093	7. **Fusion type is unrecorded in every series**, so each EMC arm mixes EWSR1::NR4A3 with whatever
1094	   TAF15::NR4A3 and rarer variants it contains, attenuating any fusion-specific signal by an unknown
1095	   amount.
1096	8. **Multiple testing is corrected for the per-gene permutation results only.** The size-matched
1097	   empirical p-values and the set-level and stratified permutation p-values remain uncorrected; the
1098	   stratified panel in particular reports five contrasts per gene on GPL6244 (three comparator
1099	   classes plus their myxoid and non-myxoid aggregations, which are not independent of the classes),
1100	   which is why §3.6 reads it on the least favourable stratum rather than the best.
1101	9. **The size-matched null is competitive and anti-conservative for coherent sets**; the exact
1102	   permutation null is self-contained but cannot make three genes into more than three genes. The two
1103	   disagree for *SEMA3C*, which is reported rather than reconciled.
1104	10. **GPL3290 is relative**, and its comparator arm spans two reference pools (§3.4). Only the
1105	    between-group contrast is interpretable, never an absolute level, and its probe→symbol mapping
1106	    runs through an EST accession bridge, so a gene unreadable there may be absent from the bridge
1107	    rather than from the array.
1108	11. **The 3SEQ rows are medians over very few peaks** — 2 (*ENO3*), 3 (*SEMA3C*), 5 (*PPARG*) — and
1109	    the percentile calibration is a rank within one deposit, not a test.
1110	12. **The covariate adjustment is a sensitivity analysis, not a correction.** If a panel gene is
1111	    itself driven by the fusion the adjustment removes real signal; that possibility is not excluded,
1112	    only made unlikely by the provenance filter.
1113	13. **The muscle control bounds differentiated-muscle admixture only**, not a myogenic programme
1114	    intrinsic to the tumour.
1115	14. **The motif scan speaks to sequence, never to occupancy**, is restricted to a fixed −10 kb/+15 kb
1116	    window, and does not reproduce the published site coordinates for either *ENO3* or *PPARG*.
1117	15. **Nothing here is an efficacy, selectivity, safety, therapeutic-window or clinical-readiness claim**
1118	    for any agent, target or gene, and expression data cannot become that evidence. No drug, dose,
1119	    schedule or patient population is named or implied.
1120	16. **The occupancy axis is measured on the wrong protein or the wrong disease, in every experiment.**
1121	    §3.11 is not evidence that these genes are unbound by the fusion. Eight of the twelve informative
1122	    experiments are NR4A1, a paralogue sharing 0.347 of its peaks with NR4A3 in matched cells; the
1123	    other four are **wild-type NR4A3 in acinic cell carcinoma**, where the protein is activated by
1124	    enhancer hijacking rather than fused, in a salivary-gland lineage that is not EMC. *PPARG*'s zero
1125	    in all four is a real negative about that setting and says nothing directly about EMC — §3.2
1126	    records native NR4A3 failing to activate the very promoter the fusion activates, so a native
1127	    cistrome is expected to disagree with a fusion one at exactly this gene. The axis bounds what
1128	    surrogates can show and nothing more.
1129	17. **The positive control and the surviving result are the same gene.** *ENO3* was designated the
1130	    instrument's positive control before any biological read (§2.4) *and* is the gene that survives
1131	    every subsequent test (§3.12). Its elevation in EMC is therefore not an independent finding of
1132	    this work — it was selected as the control because it was expected to be elevated. §3.5 sets out
1133	    why the rest of the reading is not thereby circular: the control tested one proposition, and none
1134	    of the tests that separate the three genes was part of it. The structural weakness remains, and
1135	    the observation that would remove it is a gene other than *ENO3* clearing the same bar.

1139	## 6 · Conclusion
1140	
1141	**A gene-set read on a small rare-tumour series is uninterpretable until an arbitrary set of the same
1142	size has been scored beside it on the same platform.** That is the general claim, it costs one seeded
1143	resampling, and this paper's worked example shows what it buys: the aggregate direct-target set
1144	reaches 39% and 88% of its size-matched threshold and does not clear, while the published EMC
1145	transcriptional phenotype clears the same threshold 11.9-fold and 4.2-fold on the same instrument in
1146	the same run. The instrument demonstrably reads the disease and does not read the set — a
1147	discrimination no raw contrast on these data makes, because on GPL3290 a raw contrast calls almost
1148	everything significant.
1149	
1150	Applied to the three genes, it separates what is otherwise treated alike. *ENO3* is elevated on both
1151	readable array platforms under an exact permutation test and after multiple-testing correction,
1152	against every comparator stratum separately including the myxoid-matched and reference-pool-matched
1153	arms, in the top 2% of 14,120 genes in an independent cohort on an unrelated technology, with a
1154	skeletal-muscle admixture control that does not explain it. *PPARG*'s strongest reading is circular
1155	and what remains does not survive correction; *SEMA3C* survives none of these tests and changes sign
1156	with the choice of comparator. ⚠ *ENO3* was also the pre-designated positive control, so its
1157	elevation is not an independent finding of this work (Limitation 17), and the ordering rests on
1158	cohorts of 4, 6 and 10. It is a demonstration of the instrument, not a settled result.
1159	
1160	**The binding constraint on the biology is not sample size and not statistics.** It is that class A
1161	is three genes wide, and that **no experiment has measured where an NR4A3 fusion binds, or what
1162	chromatin does, in EMC material** (§3.11 — a bounded statement about what has been deposited under a
1163	label an archive indexes, not a claim that no such data exists anywhere). The one genome-wide
1164	chromatin readout that carries NR4A3 fusions at all reads *accessibility* in HEK293T (GSE243553),
1165	not occupancy in EMC chromatin, and cannot close the gap. Nor can the existing NR4A chromatin data
1166	stand in for it: across 110 peak sets — including four deep NR4A3 cistromes in acinic cell
1167	carcinoma, a disease driven by wild-type NR4A3 — no class-A gene carries occupancy beyond a
1168	background panel. ⭐ **The sharpest form of that negative is comparative: the field performs this
1169	experiment routinely for the sibling fusions — EWSR1::WT1, EWSR1::ATF1, EWSR1::FLI1, FUS::DDIT3 and,
1170	twice, HEY1::NCOA2 — and has never performed it on EMC material.** Until it is, "up in EMC" and
1171	"driven by the fusion" cannot be told apart for any gene named here, *ENO3* included. **That
1172	experiment is specified in §4.3 and is the one thing that would change any of this.** No further
1173	correlative re-analysis of these deposits will.

## What the null controls for, and what it does not

**As the artifacts describe it.** `nr4a3-fusion-targets.json → set_scores.*.null_calibration._how`: *"4000 random gene sets of exactly N symbols drawn from this platform's own seeded null pool (4000 symbols), each scored EXACTLY as the real set is. The p-value is the fraction of draws at least as extreme, +1/+1 smoothed. It absorbs the global offset by construction: a random set carries the offset too."*

**It controls for:** (a) the platform-wide EMC-vs-comparator offset (measured `−0.0084` SD on GPL6244, `+0.0258` on GPL3290 — `platforms.*.global_offset.welch`), absorbed because a random draw carries it; (b) **set size**, drawn at exactly the observed readable size (16, 17, 19, 21 as applicable); (c) the platform's own mapped-symbol universe (18,694 / 14,932), so cross-platform probe-composition differences do not leak in.

**It does not control for:** (i) **gene–gene correlation inside a real pathway** — it permutes *genes*, not sample labels, so it is anti-conservative for coherent sets; (ii) sampling error in the *sample* dimension beyond what a size-matched draw reproduces; (iii) the comparator arm's composition; (iv) reference-pool heterogeneity on GPL3290; (v) matrix/vascular content; (vi) anything about occupancy or causation. Three further stated limits: the pool is a **seeded 4,000-symbol subsample** (21% of GPL6244's universe, 27% of GPL3290's), the same pool is reused at every set size, and the gene under test is not excluded from it. It also has a hard resolution floor (`2/4001 = 0.0005`; `2/3701 = 0.00054` for size-1 draws on GPL3290, which retain 3,700 of 4,000 draws).

**Does the prose claim more?** **No — this is the paper's strongest section.** §2.3 states the competitive/anti-conservative limit verbatim ("It is therefore anti-conservative for coherent sets and is a screen, not a test"); Figure 1's caption repeats it; Limitation 9 repeats it; the paper supplies a **separate, self-contained exact label-permutation null** (§2.6.1, enumerating all 1,623,160 and 8,008 assignments — confirmed exact in `robustness.rows[*].label_permutation.exact` = true) precisely to cover limit (i), and reports the two nulls *disagreeing* for *SEMA3C* rather than reconciling them. §3.5 also states the distinction most papers elide: *"Clearing the size-matched null says a gene's delta is extreme relative to other genes on the platform; it is not the same statement as the two arms differing for that gene."* §3.9 then applies the null against the paper's own headline set and reports the refusal at a quantified distance (39% and 88%).

**On the campaign-level lane-2 finding.** `COMMON-BRIEF.md` records that on `emc-expression-panels.json` the arm-to-arm `E1` limb fires for 0.2950 of random 14-gene panels against a nominal 0.05, attributed to a gene-set-independent offset between the EMC arm's six GPL6244 arrays and the LGFMS arrays. That is a measurement about a **different instrument** (W02i/j's frozen arm-to-arm rule on the panels artifact), not about this paper's competitive null, which is drawn from the same arrays as the observed set and absorbs any such offset by construction — and this paper measures that offset directly and finds it an order of magnitude below the effects in question. I record the adjacency without importing the lane-2 verdict onto this null; no lane-2 statistics were run.

**Repo-curated-panel check (the second named failure mode).** The paper scores no group from `emc-expression-panels.json`; it cites that file only as `→ gene_reads`, an independent second implementation of the **per-gene** array reads (Data-and-code table; corroborated by `controls.checks.positive_control_ENO3.expect`, which names that leaf as the one home of the committed *ENO3* prior). The two covariate panels (11 structural, 3 vascular) live in `nr4a3-fusion-targets-confounds.json → provenance_audit.panels` and are described in §2.6.3 exactly as what they are — a provenance-filtered selection made by this work, explicitly "a sensitivity analysis, not a correction". Set D is a **published** list (`set_definitions.D_filion_table1_emc_vs_137_sarcomas.citation` — Filion 2009 Table 1) and §3.9 explicitly denies it is a fusion-target set. The 198-gene occupancy background is described as "assembled for an unrelated question", which the artifact confirms (`background_panel._why_this_panel`). **No repo-curated group is presented as a published signature.**

**Cohort/platform-vs-disease check (the third named failure mode).** §2.2, Figure 3's caption and Limitation 2 all state the three cohorts are never pooled and that the platforms measure different quantities. §2.2's ⚠ block correctly identifies **GSE170983 as the same Brunner deposit as GSE28866** and says counting them separately "would raise the apparent EMC total to 24 without adding a patient"; §2.2 also records that GSE28866's 32 libraries come from **30 specimens** because of two technical-replicate pairs. §3.13's SRA block refuses to read `EWSR1`-negative as "not EMC". I found **no** instance of two arrays or two specimen labels being asserted to be different patients.

## Limitations

- I verified numbers against **committed artifacts**, not against the raw deposits. An artifact and the manuscript agreeing does not establish that either reads GEO correctly; that would need a producer run, which my dispatch forbids and which I did not do.
- Two quantities were **not checked** and remain UNKNOWN rather than verified: the hg19/hg38 panel-recovery figures (90.6–93.9% vs 32.2–33.6%) behind the Haller build call, and the "53–154 peaks / 0.0%" range for the twelve ChIP-Atlas NR4A3 sets. The "*VCAM1* significantly down on both" claim was not re-derived. "7 series to 22" was not separately re-derived.
- **Absence of a located source is not evidence a claim is false.** D5's upper bound and D6's 0.347 are graded NO SOURCE LOCATED, not refuted.
- I made no scientific judgement about whether *ENO3* is a fusion target, and none of this bears on efficacy, safety, selectivity, therapeutic window or clinical readiness for any agent, target or gene. There is no wet lab and I ran none.
- This verdict is specific to PUB-FUSION-OUTPUT. It is **not** a readiness claim about this manuscript or any other, no repository census was taken, and no other paper was assessed.
- No content-policy refusal was encountered in this run.

**Overall reading, stated plainly:** the paper's own null is described accurately and conservatively, the title's concession is honoured in every downstream claim I could check, no repo-curated group is passed off as a published signature, no cohort or platform difference is read as a disease difference, and the one place a missing measurement leaks into a stated number is D5 (and, less severely, D6). The seven defects are prose-level and all are repairable without touching a number in §3.
